transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM), Sanjay (Kestrel HoM), Lina (Kestrel Platform), Tom (Kestrel CTO), Rachel (Kestrel Procurement)

Summary (auto): brief review of December cost spike, two short latency regressions on route /chat/agent, proposal to run quantized benchmarks and rightsizing plan, discuss Dedicated pilot timeline.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you see my screen? uh, i think we are just on audio, that's fine. quick agenda, go over usage, cost, incidents, and a short roadmap alignment.
[00:28] Sanjay: yep, thanks Maya. real quick, wanted to flag — December was pretty gnarly for us, we saw token spend up 3x week-over-week when the new feature rolled out. wanted to understand if that's purely usage or if we ran into inefficiencies.
[00:45] Owen: yeah, we pulled the telemetry — looks like two things: longer prefix sizes on the chat endpoints, and some requests falling back to a heavier model during a provisioning spike. the KV cache wasn't hit for some of your multi-turn flows, maybe due to session id differences.
[01:10] Lina: when you say "KV cash" do you mean the K-V cache? we've got sticky session handling but maybe the client is rotating a header.
[01:22] Owen: yeah K-V cache, sorry the transcript's, um, sometimes the auto caption does that. so the cache keys didn't align for ~25% of flows during the surge. that increased tokening and compute.
[01:40] Tom: is that on Hosted or Dedicated? we're evaluating Dedicated because we want predictable throughput, but we also don't want to overcommit.
[01:50] Maya: right now it's hosted. Dedicated pilot has been discussed — there's a middle ground too, reserved capacity bursts. we can model cost vs latency for both.
[02:08] Rachel: procurement question — if we go Dedicated, how do billing and overages work? need clarity for legal.
[02:17] Diego: we can provide a pricing sheet and examples; typically it's a committed monthly capacity with defined burst and overage rates. i'll follow up with the exact contract language.
[02:35] Sanjay: there were also two latency incidents Jan 3rd and Jan 10th — i saw fallbacks to a smaller region and an A/B rollback. can you summarize root cause?
[02:49] Owen: quick tl;dr: Jan 3rd was a transient node OOM that triggered autoscaler to spin new nodes; some in-flight requests routed to a lower-capacity model as a fallback. Jan 10th was a networking blip in the eu-west region, which caused slightly elevated p95 for ~12 minutes. both were mitigated by automatic fallback policies but we can tighten thresholds.
[03:18] Sanjay: mitigation is fine, but we need clearer SLO reports tied to incidents. Diego, can you include the incident timeline?
[03:24] Diego: yes, i'll attach the timeline and the debug trace.
[03:30] [Speaker 1]: quick question, any security impact?
[03:35] Maya: no data was exfiltrated, audit logs were preserved, and no infra change was required. standard post-incident review is logged.
[03:44] Lina: on cost, we noticed embeddings usage spiked too. are you suggesting different model families or quantization?
[03:52] Owen: for embeddings we usually recommend switching to a smaller embedding model for similarity-only workloads; for chat generation we can test int8 and int4 quantized variants. quantization often reduces memory and cost but we should validate quality.
[04:12] Sanjay: can we get a benchmark on our top 10 prompts? that's what we'd care about.
[04:18] Owen: absolutely — if you share the prompt set we'll run latency and log-prob checks between fp16, int8, and int4.
[04:28] Maya: that's one of the next steps — Owen will do the benchmark, Diego will pull cost per route, and i'll put together a rightsizing proposal.
[04:39] Tom: curious about the Console's per-token breakout — is that at the route level or per-user?
[04:45] Diego: Console shows per-route and per-model cost. we can also export token-level traces per API key if you want to slice by user.
[04:55] Rachel: procurement: we need an example PO and an SLA addendum.
[04:59] Maya: we can share sample contract language and the SLA metrics — i'll include the typical uptime, p95 latency targets, and incident response SLA.
[05:12] Sanjay: what's the projected savings if we quantize and move some traffic to a smaller model? rough ballpark.
[05:20] Owen: ballpark — depends on traffic shape. for generation-heavy endpoints, quantizing to int8 can save 20-30% on GPU time; int4 could add another 10% but with more quality checks. offloading embeddings to a smaller family often saves 40-60% on embedding spend.
[05:44] Lina: any impact on latencies — does quantization increase infer time?
[05:49] Owen: sometimes slightly higher per-token latency on certain GPU kernels but overall throughput and cost improve; we can find kernel/config combos that keep p95 acceptable.
[06:10] Sanjay: roadmap items — we plan a product increment in March that will double our multi-turn chat volume; we need a capacity plan.
[06:20] Maya: given that, we suggest a staged Dedicated pilot: 4-week pilot on a mid-tier Dedicated pool with defined ingress to measure tail latencies and cost. at end of pilot we'll recommend commit levels.
[06:37] Tom: how quickly can we stand up the Dedicated pilot?
[06:40] Diego: usually 2-3 weeks for config + network setup assuming no additional compliance hurdles. if you need VPC peering or HSM/KMS integration that can add time.
[06:54] Rachel: we do require KMS integration for key management for any persistent logs, that's a must.
[07:02] Maya: noted — our Private deployment options support customer-managed KMS and audit logging. we'll include matrix of options.
[07:12] Sanjay: what about routing policies — can we route by latency vs cost or by customer segment?
[07:18] Owen: yes, smart routing supports policies: lowest-latency, cost-preferred, or hybrid rules. you can also pin specific users to dedicated pools.
[07:32] Lina: we saw some misrouting in December during the spike — requests were split across regions unexpectedly. is that likely config drift?
[07:40] Owen: likely either a policy parameter or a health check flapping metric; we'll add more guarded routing rules for your critical routes.
[07:52] Sanjay: SLA question — do you provide credits or reconciliation for degraded minutes?
[07:58] Diego: SLA credits can be applied per contract; i'll share the typical formula in the follow-up.
[08:06] [00:08:06] Maya: okay, quick recap of concrete items: rightsizing proposal, per-route cost export, quantization benchmarks on top prompts, sample PO + SLA language, and timeline for Dedicated pilot.
[08:20] Tom: can the rightsizing proposal include a conservative and aggressive plan? we like to see both.
[08:25] Maya: yes two scenarios: conservative (minimal risk) and aggressive (higher savings, test gating).
[08:33] Rachel: procurement will need a list of contacts and the contract template to start internal approvals.
[08:38] Diego: i'll include contact list and a redline-friendly template.
[08:45] Sanjay: any blockers on the engineering side for the pilot? we need to know if we'll need to change session ids or routing headers.
[08:53] Owen: minimal client changes if you stick to a consistent session key; we'll send a small client lint tool to validate keys and highlight cache misses.
[09:05] Lina: when you run benchmarks, can you also include memory footprint so we can anticipate instance sizing?
[09:12] Owen: yes, we'll capture GPU memory, latency, and throughput.
[09:20] Maya: what about compliance — SOC2/ISO — do you need evidence?
[09:25] Rachel: we already requested SOC2 docs; happy to get the packet.
[09:30] Diego: sending SOC2 + SOC3 and network diagrams in follow-up.
[09:36] Sanjay: one more thing — can we do a cost guardrail in Console that auto-throttles non-critical routes if spend exceeds a threshold?
[09:45] Maya: Console supports cost alerts and automated throttling policies; we'll show a sample policy and defaults.
[09:52] Tom: curious about regression monitoring tied to prompt sets — will Redwood optimize alert on quality drift?
[09:59] Owen: Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set evals and alert on distributional drift or quality regressions tied to rollout changes. we can wire that to your slack channel.
[10:10] Sanjay: great — please sig up for the follow-ups.
[10:14] Maya: agreed. any other questions?
[10:18] [crosstalk] Lina: nothing else.
[10:22] Maya: ok final recap — i'll send the rightsizing proposal & sample contract, Owen will run quantization benchmarks, Diego will export cost breakdown and incident timeline, Rachel will confirm PO timeline. we'll aim to reconvene with a pilot kickoff in 2-3 weeks.
[10:40] Tom: thanks everyone.
[10:42] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcription includes occasional mislabels and typos due to auto captions ( e.g., K-V cash ). Links referenced during call: [Redwood rightsizing template] (link shared), [Quant benchmark spreadsheet] (to be shared), [Incident timeline doc] (will be in follow-up).
